model_annotation: Figure 5 presents two line plots, (a) Loss vs. training steps and (b) Loss vs. training FLOPs, illustrating the training loss curves for different model configurations trained from scratch. Both plots share the same y-axis, labeled "Loss," which is scaled logarithmically and ranges from 0.01 to 10.0, with tick labels at intervals of 0.1, 1.0, and 10.0. The x-axis in plot (a) is labeled "Training steps" and spans from 0 to 500,000, with tick marks at intervals of 100,000. In plot (b), the x-axis is labeled "Training FLOPs" and ranges from 0 to 500,000, with tick marks at intervals of 100,000. The plot displays five distinct lines, each corresponding to a different model variant: Vanilla (solid black line), Strm.LM (n=380) (dashed red line), Sep.LLM (n=64) (dotted blue line), Sep.LLM (n=128) (dash-dotted green line), and Sep.LLM (n=64,H/T) (dash-dot-dotted purple line). In both plots, the Vanilla model starts with a loss of approximately 1.0 and decreases to around 0.1 by 500,000 steps or FLOPs. The Strm.LM (n=380) model begins at a loss of approximately 1.0 and decreases to around 0.1 by 500,000 steps or FLOPs. The Sep.LLM (n=64) model begins at a loss of approximately 1.0 and decreases to around 0.1 by 500,000 steps or FLOPs. The Sep.LLM (n=128) model begins at a loss of approximately 1.0 and decreases to around 0.1 by 500,000 steps or FLOPs. The Sep.LLM (n=64,H/T) model begins at a loss of approximately 1.0 and decreases to around 0.1 by 500,000 steps or FLOPs.
